title: D-dimer
subtitle: Fibrin degradation product for thromboembolism screening
summary: D-dimer measurement for assessment of thromboembolic risk and exclusion of venous thromboembolism in low-risk patients.
introduction: D-dimer is a fibrin degradation product released when fibrin is broken down by plasmin. It is raised in thromboembolism but also in many other conditions (infection, inflammation, malignancy, trauma, DIC). Use as a rule-out test only in low-risk patients; never use to rule in thromboembolism.

rows.name: D-dimer
lowInterpretation: Normal D-dimer: thromboembolism excluded in LOW-risk patients using validated clinical score (Wells score ≤2). No further investigation needed.
highInterpretation: Elevated D-dimer (≥500 ng/mL): Non-specific finding. Seen in DVT/PE but also infection, inflammation, malignancy, trauma. Interpretation depends on clinical pretest probability.
LOW pretest probability (Wells ≤2): elevated D-dimer with high-sensitivity assay still excludes PE; if >500 ng/mL or lower-sensitivity assay, imaging (CTPA) required.
INTERMEDIATE/HIGH pretest probability: imaging (CT PE protocol or ultrasound for DVT) mandatory regardless of D-dimer; never rely on D-dimer alone.
Pregnancy: D-dimer often elevated physiologically; imaging preferred over D-dimer interpretation.
notes: Age-adjusted thresholds (patient age × 10 ng/mL) may improve specificity in older adults but should be used cautiously.
Serial D-dimer testing not recommended; single measurement is sufficient.
Most useful in emergency department with validated clinical scoring systems.

urgentFindings: D-dimer >500 ng/mL + high pretest probability of PE or DVT: urgent imaging (CTPA or compression ultrasound) required.
D-dimer normal + LOW pretest probability: PE/DVT excluded; safe discharge.
D-dimer elevated + pregnancy/cancer/recent surgery: always proceed to imaging regardless of D-dimer value.
overrides: Never use D-dimer to confirm thromboembolism; use only to exclude in low-risk patients.
Do not order D-dimer in asymptomatic patients without clinical indication.
Age-adjusted thresholds may improve specificity but should not delay imaging in high-risk patients.

commonPatterns.title: Suspected PE in low-risk patient
actions: If D-dimer <500 ng/mL: PE excluded, safe discharge
If D-dimer ≥500 ng/mL: CT PE protocol required

commonPatterns.title: Suspected DVT (leg pain/swelling)
actions: If D-dimer ≥500 ng/mL: compression ultrasound (both legs) required

commonPatterns.title: Incidental elevated D-dimer (no VTE symptoms)
findings: D-dimer sent for other reasons (sepsis workup)
D-dimer elevated but no PE/DVT symptoms
No leg pain, dyspnoea, or chest pain
interpretation: Consider other causes: infection, inflammation, malignancy, trauma
No imaging for PE/DVT if asymptomatic
actions: Investigate other causes (CRP, infection, malignancy screen)
Reassure patient if no VTE symptoms

rationale: Persistent PE symptoms despite normal D-dimer in high-risk patient

furtherTesting.test: Blood cultures, CRP, imaging for malignancy
rationale: If elevated D-dimer with no thromboembolism features
Consider DIC if severely elevated (PT, aPTT, fibrinogen, platelet count)
